q: India won the men's cricket gold at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan. Which team did India beat in the final on 3 October 2026?
exp: India made 211-6 and won the final in Nagoya by 19 runs after Pakistan finished on 192-6. It was India's second Asian Games men's gold in a row.

q: Which team did India beat in the women's cricket final at the 2026 Asian Games on 22 September 2026?
exp: India won by 147 runs and kept their Asian Games gold medal. Sri Lanka took silver and Pakistan took bronze.

q: What is the theme of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign?
exp: The theme stresses shared ownership, youth involvement and steady cleanliness habits. The Swachh Bharat Mission began on 2 October 2014, and 2 October is marked as Swachh Bharat Diwas.

q: On which date did the Constitution of India come into effect?
exp: The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, which India celebrates as Republic Day. It was adopted earlier, on 26 November 1949.

q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
exp: Jupiter is the largest planet. About 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

q: Which planet is often called the Red Planet?
exp: Mars looks red because iron minerals in its soil and dust have rusted.

q: India won the Women's Asia Cup in September 2026. How many titles has India now won in the tournament?
exp: India beat Sri Lanka in the final on 13 September 2026 and went through the tournament unbeaten, a record-extending eighth title.

q: India's retail inflation based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for August 2026 was about how much?

q: What is the name of India's own independent satellite navigation system, earlier called IRNSS?

q: Who wrote the song Jana Gana Mana, which is India's national anthem?
exp: Rabindranath Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana in Bengali. The Constituent Assembly adopted it as the national anthem on 24 January 1950.

q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which Indian state?
exp: The Thar Desert is in north-western India, partly in Rajasthan, and also extends into eastern Pakistan.

q: On which date did the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya close?
exp: The closing ceremony is on 4 October 2026.

q: World Space Week 2026 runs from 4 to 10 October. The 4 October date marks the 1957 launch of which satellite?

q: India's gross GST collections for September 2026 were about how much?

q: India won the men's hockey gold at the 2026 Asian Games on 3 October. Which team did India beat in the final?

q: A new Vande Bharat Express was flagged off on 2 October 2026 between Surat and Udaipur. Which two states does it connect?

q: On 3 October 2026, Russia hit a second major bridge in which capital city?

q: In which Indian town was Mahatma Gandhi born, on 2 October 1869?

q: Which institutions does PM-SETU focus on upgrading, according to the PIB update of 3 October 2026?
exp: PM-SETU is a vocational-skills programme focused on modernising Government ITIs and making their training more relevant to industry.

q: According to the PIB update of 4 October 2026, how many supercomputers had India deployed under the National Supercomputing Mission by September 2026?

q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, announced on 5 October, recognises discoveries behind which method?
exp: The Nobel Assembly awarded Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, a method for controlling nerve signals with light.

q: What is the theme of World Space Week 2026, according to UN News on 4 October?
exp: The dated UN News article names Rocket revolution as the 2026 theme, focusing on changes in how people reach space.

q: Which green pigment in plants absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
exp: Chlorophyll is a key pigment involved in photosynthesis. It absorbs light energy used by plants to make food.

q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
exp: The Pacific is the largest ocean and covers about one-third of Earth's surface.

q: Which observatory is named in the citation for the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics announced on 6 October?

exp: The heart has two atria and two ventricles, making four chambers.

q: Which two elements make up water?

q: What is the name of the first indigenous Fleet Support Ship launched at Hindustan Shipyard in Visakhapatnam on 6 October 2026?

q: What was the official slogan of the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, according to PIB on 6 October?
exp: The PIB overview dated 6 October identifies Imagine One Asia as the official slogan of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games.

q: The PIB factsheet of 17 September 2026 describes ECMS as a scheme supporting manufacturing of what?
exp: ECMS means Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme. The dated factsheet describes support for India's electronic-component production.

q: The El Nino pattern discussed by UN News on 6 October is linked to unusual warming in which ocean?
exp: UN News describes the El Nino pattern in the tropical Pacific and how it can change rainfall far away. This question does not ask for a forecast outcome.

q: The femur is the bone in which part of the human body?
exp: The femur is the upper leg bone, joining the hip and knee.

q: Which gas do green plants use from the air during photosynthesis?
exp: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water, with light energy, to produce sugars and release oxygen.

q: Who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on 8 October?
exp: The official Nobel homepage names Canadian author Anne Carson. The announcement was also reported by BBC on 8 October.

q: What is the theme of India Mobile Congress 2026, according to PIB on 5 October?

q: A PIB report on 2 October described a tigress release at Buxa Tiger Reserve. In which state is Buxa?
exp: The dated wildlife release locates Buxa Tiger Reserve in West Bengal and describes a phased tiger reintroduction programme.

q: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere?
exp: NASA describes the air mixture as about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen. Nitrogen therefore makes up the largest share.

q: During evaporation, liquid water changes into what?
exp: Evaporation changes water from liquid into gas at the surface. Water vapour is the gaseous form of water.

q: Who was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on 9 October?
exp: The Norwegian Nobel Committee named Navi Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law. UN News independently reported the announcement.

q: Which city was named for the second Sadhana Shrinkhla regional workshop scheduled for 9 October 2026?

q: Which city hosts the third International Bharat 6G Symposium, according to PIB on 8 October?
exp: The dated telecom release places the symposium at Yashobhoomi in Dwarka, New Delhi, from 7 to 9 October.

q: The National Medical Library conference reported by PIB on 9 October focused on access to which resources?
exp: The conference theme was Digital Health Resources: Redefining Access Through Libraries. It focused on medical knowledge and digital resources.

q: The Great Indian Bustard release reported by PIB on 4 October took place in Desert National Park in which state?
exp: The owning wildlife release places the release of two male Great Indian Bustards at Sam, Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.

q: How many sides does a triangle have?
exp: A triangle is a polygon formed by three line segments.

q: Which organs take oxygen from inhaled air into the blood?
exp: The lungs exchange gases: oxygen enters the blood and carbon dioxide leaves it.

q: Which toll-free number for Tele-MANAS mental health support was highlighted by PIB on 9 October 2026?
exp: The dated health ministry release identifies 14416 as the Tele-MANAS national toll-free helpline for confidential mental health support.

q: On which date was World Post Day observed in 2026, according to the PIB report of 9 October?
exp: World Post Day is observed on 9 October. The PIB report connects it with the founding of the Universal Postal Union in 1874.

q: Which organisation conducted the cyclone warning and marine weather services workshop reported by PIB on 9 October?
exp: PIB names the India Meteorological Department as the workshop organiser. The training covered cyclone warnings and marine weather services.

q: Which international organisation jointly organised the AI for Good Lab workshop with India's Department of Telecommunications on 9 October 2026?
exp: The dated telecom release names the International Telecommunication Union, or ITU, as the joint organiser with the Department of Telecommunications.

q: The PIB announcement of 9 October placed the Finance Minister's official visit from 9 to 11 October 2026 in which country?
exp: The announcement places the official visit in Singapore. It lists meetings on investment and the India-Singapore partnership; the question asks the announced destination.

q: How many square faces does a cube have?
exp: A cube has six square faces. Its eight corners and twelve edges are different counts.

q: About how long does Earth take to complete one orbit around the Sun?
exp: NASA gives about 365.25 days for one trip around the Sun. That is about one year; one day is the time for Earth's rotation.

q: According to the PIB factsheet of 10 October 2026, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana focuses on how many agricultural districts?
exp: The dated factsheet describes focused agricultural development across 100 Aspirational Agricultural Districts.

q: The PIB lighthouse feature of 10 October places the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal in which state?
exp: The feature locates Lothal and the planned National Maritime Heritage Complex in Gujarat. It describes a lighthouse museum as part of the complex.

q: The PIB announcement of 10 October scheduled the Defence Secretary's 12-15 October visit to which pair of countries?
exp: The announcement names Cyprus and Greece. The question asks the announced destinations, not whether the visit has happened.

q: The PIB announcement of 10 October places the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at which institute?
exp: PIB identifies the brain research centre as being at IIT Madras. The announced programme includes mapping human brains into detailed atlases.

q: At which city's Air Force Station did the Defence Minister address Tarang Shakti participants on 10 October 2026?
exp: The dated release places the address at Air Force Station Jodhpur during the multinational air exercise.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
exp: The heart acts as the muscular pump of the circulatory system, moving blood through the body.

q: What happens when the north poles of two magnets are brought close together?
exp: Like magnetic poles repel. Unlike poles, such as north and south, attract.

q: The PIB announcement of 10 October places the Prime Minister's 11 October programme, including the IIT Madras Brain Centre, in which city?
exp: The dated announcement places the programme in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. It is an announced programme, not a claim that all events have finished.

q: Which Indian armed service hosts the multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti, described by PIB on 10 October 2026?
exp: Tarang Shakti is a multinational air exercise hosted by the Indian Air Force. Air exercise is the clue linking the event to the service.

q: After which conquest did Emperor Ashoka renounce armed conquest and favour rule through dharma?
exp: The suffering caused by the Kalinga conquest led Ashoka to renounce armed conquest. The other battles belong to much later periods.

q: Which Indian state is the largest by area?
exp: The Rajasthan government identifies Rajasthan as the largest Indian state by area. Area and population are different measures.

q: Which instrument measures the relative density of a liquid?
exp: A hydrometer measures relative density. Thermometers measure temperature, barometers pressure, and anemometers wind speed.

q: Who were named as the two 2026 Economic Sciences laureates in the official announcement on 12 October?
ans: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford
d: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
Kenneth J. Arrow and Paul A. Samuelson
exp: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences named Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for work improving stabilisation policy. This asks the laureate pair, not the technical theory.

q: Which Indian body announced its 33rd Foundation Day function for 12 October 2026?
exp: The dated PIB announcement identifies the National Human Rights Commission, India, whose Foundation Day function was planned for 12 October. NHRC works to protect and promote human rights.

q: Which imaginary line divides Earth into the Northern and Southern hemispheres?
exp: The Equator is the line at zero degrees latitude. It divides Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.

q: Which pigment in green plants absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
exp: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy used in photosynthesis. It is found in the chloroplasts of green plants.

q: Emperor Ashoka belonged to which ancient Indian dynasty?
exp: Ashoka ruled the Mauryan empire. His rock and pillar edicts give evidence about his reign and policies.

q: Which House of India's Parliament is called the House of the People?
exp: Lok Sabha means House of the People. Rajya Sabha is the Council of States. Parliament includes the President and both Houses.

q: Which institution issues India's Rs500 banknotes?
d: Securities and Exchange Board of India
exp: The Reserve Bank of India issues banknotes such as Rs500. Do not confuse banknotes with coins or the special Rs1 note, which are issued by the Government of India.

q: What is the focus of WHO's World Mental Health Day 2026 theme, "Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change"?
exp: WHO calls for people with lived experience to help shape policies, services and decisions about mental health care.

q: In which city were electric buses flagged off and new air-quality monitoring stations inaugurated on 13 October 2026?
exp: PIB reported the bus flag-off at Anand Vihar and the inauguration of air-quality monitoring stations across Delhi on 13 October.

q: The stratospheric ozone layer protects life mainly by absorbing which radiation from the Sun?
exp: Stratospheric ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation. It does not block all sunlight.

q: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta opens into which body of water?
exp: The Ganges and Brahmaputra reach the Bay of Bengal through their delta. The Arabian Sea lies on the other side of India.

q: Which feature is strongly associated with the cities of the Indus civilization?
exp: Indus cities such as Mohenjo-daro had brick-built bathrooms and drainage. The other features belong to much later traditions.

q: Under Article 51A, protecting the natural environment and showing compassion for living creatures is a:
exp: Article 51A(g) lists this among the Fundamental Duties of citizens. Duties, rights and Directive Principles are separate constitutional categories.

q: Which instrument would you use to check whether a liquid has become hotter?
exp: A thermometer measures temperature. A hydrometer measures relative density, a barometer pressure and an anemometer wind speed.

q: The 2026 International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction theme, "Resilience Starts at Home", places which setting at the centre of preparedness?
exp: UNDRR selected Resilience Starts at Home for the day observed on 13 October 2026. It focuses on safer housing and household preparedness.

q: Which UN agency is organising the World Food Day global ceremony scheduled for 16 October 2026 under "Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow."?
exp: FAO announced the ceremony at its headquarters for 16 October 2026. FAO is the Food and Agriculture Organization; the ceremony was still upcoming when this test was prepared.

q: Why would a ringing bell inside a container become harder to hear as the air is removed?
exp: Sound is a mechanical vibration carried by matter. With less air to carry it, less sound reaches a listener; sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

q: Which pair of seas is connected by the Suez Canal?
d: Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
exp: The Suez Canal runs through Egypt and connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.

q: The rock-cut temples and monasteries at Ajanta are primarily associated with which religion?
exp: Ajanta is a group of Buddhist cave temples and monasteries in Maharashtra, celebrated for its paintings. Do not confuse it with the mixed religious traditions at Ellora.

q: Article 324 gives the superintendence, direction and control of parliamentary elections to which body?
exp: Article 324 vests these election responsibilities in the Election Commission. The other institutions have different constitutional functions.

q: If prices rise while a person's money income stays unchanged, what usually happens to that income's purchasing power?
exp: The unchanged income buys fewer goods and services when prices rise. Inflation therefore reduces its purchasing power.

q: PIB's 14 October announcement places a new Leh airport passenger terminal in which part of India?
exp: PIB announced the Leh terminal as part of development projects in Ladakh scheduled for 15 October. This question uses the announcement, not a claim that the inauguration had already finished.

q: On which date was the UN International Day of the Girl Child observed in October 2026?
exp: The UN marks International Day of the Girl Child on 11 October. The 2026 observance called for investment in girls' rights.

q: Which organs filter wastes and extra water from the blood to form urine?
exp: The kidneys filter blood and remove wastes and extra water as urine. The bladder stores urine after it has been made.

q: The Palk Strait lies between India and which neighbouring country?
exp: The Palk Strait separates southeastern India from northern Sri Lanka.

q: Which battle in 1757 brought Robert Clive's East India Company forces into conflict with Siraj al-Dawlah of Bengal?
exp: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757. Clive led the East India Company forces against the forces of Siraj al-Dawlah.

q: What is the minimum age an otherwise eligible Indian citizen must have reached on the qualifying date to register as a voter?
exp: The Election Commission states that a citizen must have attained 18 years on the qualifying date. Citizenship, ordinary residence and other eligibility requirements also apply.

q: Which currency would normally be used to pay in a shop in Japan?
exp: Japan's currency is the yen. The Bank of Japan lists its notes and coins in yen.
src: Bank of Japan, notes and coins

q: Whose birth anniversary did President Droupadi Murmu mark with floral tributes on 15 October 2026?
exp: The President's official photo record identifies the tribute at Vijayawada on 15 October 2026 as one to former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

q: On which date did the UN mark the International Day of Rural Women in 2026?
exp: UN Women's statement of 13 October identifies the International Day of Rural Women as 15 October 2026. It recognises rural women's contributions to farming, communities and nature.

q: At standard sea-level atmospheric pressure, what is the approximate boiling point of pure water?
exp: Water boils at about 100 degrees Celsius at standard sea-level pressure. Its boiling point is lower at higher altitudes because the pressure is lower.

q: The Prime Meridian is the reference line for which value?
exp: A prime meridian is chosen as zero degrees longitude. Zero degrees latitude is the Equator. The historic Greenwich line and modern satellite reference meridian are slightly apart.

q: The 1930 Dandi March challenged British laws controlling which everyday product?
exp: Gandhi and his followers went to Dandi and broke the British salt law by collecting salt. The march was part of civil disobedience against colonial rule.

q: Which institution is at the top of India's judicial system?
exp: The Supreme Court of India is the apex judicial body under the Constitution. High Courts and district-level courts are below it in the judicial system.

q: Which sport uses a shuttlecock rather than a ball during play?
exp: Badminton players hit a shuttlecock across a net with lightweight rackets. The other listed sports use balls.

q: The UN message for 17 October 2026 linked "Safe Homes for All" to which international day?
ans: International Day for the Eradication of Poverty
d: International Day of Persons with Disabilities
International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction
exp: The Secretary-General message dated 16 October names 17 October 2026 as the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty. Its theme links safe, affordable homes with reducing poverty.

q: Which organisation launched the nationwide Green Diwali Campaign on 20 October 2026?
exp: PIB on 20 October 2026 names WWF-India EIACP as the campaign organiser. Its Programme Centre is supported by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The campaign urges a cracker-free Diwali.

q: Which tiny openings in leaves allow gases to move between the leaf and the air?
exp: Stomata are pores in the leaf surface. They allow gas exchange and are opened or closed by guard cells.

q: A map marks a latitude about 23.5 degrees north. Which named line is it?
exp: The Tropic of Cancer is about 23.5 degrees north of the Equator. The Tropic of Capricorn is at the corresponding southern latitude.

q: Emperor Akbar belonged to which ruling dynasty?
exp: Akbar was a Mughal emperor. The Maurya and Gupta dynasties ruled much earlier, while the Cholas were a southern dynasty.

q: Under Article 32, a person can move the Supreme Court directly to enforce which of these?
exp: Article 32 provides the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. The Court can issue appropriate directions, orders or writs.

q: What is the purpose of the thin wire inside an electrical fuse?
ans: To melt and break the circuit if current is excessive
d: To store charge and release it when current stops
To increase voltage when a circuit is overloaded
To keep current flowing when a wire is damaged
exp: A fuse uses a metal strip or wire that melts when current exceeds its intended level. The break interrupts the circuit and helps protect it.

q: Sirpur, an ancient site in the news for joining UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list, is in which Indian state?
exp: UNESCO's tentative list carries the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh, on the Mahanadi river. Its addition was reported on 20 October 2026.

q: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement came into force on 20 October 2026. What access does it give Indian exports to New Zealand?
exp: The agreement gives 100 percent of Indian exports duty-free entry into the New Zealand market, as reported on 20 October 2026.

q: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
exp: About 78 percent of the air is nitrogen. Oxygen is about 21 percent.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
exp: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert. Antarctica is a larger cold desert, which is why the question says hot desert.

q: Who wrote the song that became India's national anthem?
exp: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', adopted as the national anthem. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', the national song.

q: Who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal?
exp: Abhinav Bindra won the men's 10 metre air rifle event at the Beijing 2008 Olympics, India's first individual gold.

q: Which institution has the sole right to issue currency notes in India?
exp: The Reserve Bank of India is the sole authority for issuing currency notes, except the one-rupee note issued by the Government of India.
src: Reserve Bank of India, currency management

q: Researchers discovered three new species of which creature in the Western Ghats forests of Kerala and Karnataka, as reported on 20 October 2026?
exp: Zoological Survey of India's Western Ghats Regional Centre and Malabar Christian College named Rhysida quadrispinosa, Rhysida coorgensis and Rhysida neyyarensis, taking India's Rhysida species count to 23. Reported 20 October 2026.

q: AUSTRAHIND 2026, a joint military exercise that began in Kerala on 19 October 2026, is held between India and which country?
exp: The 5th edition of AUSTRAHIND runs from 19 October to 1 November 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, with about 240 personnel from India and Australia. Reported 19 October 2026.

q: What is the sum of the three interior angles of any triangle?
exp: The three angles inside any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.

q: Which star is nearest to the Earth?
exp: The Sun is our nearest star, about 150 million kilometres away. The Moon is not a star, and Mars is a planet.

q: Which vitamin does sunlight help our skin make?
exp: Sunlight on the skin helps the body make vitamin D, which keeps bones strong.

q: The Eiffel Tower stands in which city?
exp: The Eiffel Tower has stood in Paris, France, since 1889.

q: Who wrote the Harry Potter books?
exp: J.K. Rowling wrote the seven Harry Potter novels, published between 1997 and 2007.

q: At the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, India's Sheetal Devi won two gold medals on 22 October 2026 in which sport?
exp: Sheetal Devi won two gold medals in archery at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya, Japan, as reported on 22 October 2026.

q: ISRO's NVS-03 navigation satellite has been cleared for a launch attempt on 30 October 2026. NVS-03 will join which Indian satellite navigation system?
exp: ISRO indicated on 22 October 2026 that NVS-03 is cleared for a launch attempt on 30 October from Sriharikota. NVS satellites form India's own NavIC system; GPS is American, Galileo European and GLONASS Russian.

q: Which animal is traditionally called the 'Ship of the Desert'?
exp: The camel is called the Ship of the Desert because it can carry people and loads across dry deserts for days without water.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
exp: A leap year has 366 days; the extra day is 29 February. It keeps the calendar in step with Earth's journey around the Sun.

q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
exp: Australia is the smallest continent; Asia is the largest.

q: How many colours are there in a rainbow?
exp: A rainbow shows seven colours: violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red.
src: NCERT Class 10 Science, The Human Eye and the Colourful World

q: Which festival is known as the Festival of Lights?
exp: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is celebrated with rows of lamps and candles; it falls in October or November.

q: The Prime Meridian, which passes through Greenwich, marks the zero point for which measurement?
exp: Longitude is measured east and west from the Prime Meridian at Greenwich, counted as 0 degrees. The zero line for latitude is the Equator. The historic Greenwich line and the modern satellite reference meridian differ slightly.

q: Which state's Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape was added to UNESCO's tentative World Heritage list, as reported on 20 October 2026?
exp: Sirpur village lies in the Mahasamund district of Chhattisgarh, on the Mahanadi river, and is a nationally protected monument. The UNESCO tentative-list addition was reported on 20 October 2026.

q: Since the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement took effect on 20 October 2026, what duty applies to Indian goods exported to New Zealand?
exp: New Zealand now gives 100% duty-free market access covering all tariff lines and all of India's current exports, The Hindu reported on 20 October 2026.

q: 'Jana Gana Mana', India's national anthem, was written by which famous poet?
exp: Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', later adopted as India's national anthem. 'Vande Mataram', the national song, was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: Rhysida quadrispinosa, Rhysida coorgensis and Rhysida neyyarensis, newly discovered in the Western Ghats, are three new species of which creature?
exp: The discoveries in Kerala and Karnataka forests, by ZSI's Western Ghats Regional Centre and Malabar Christian College, bring India's known Rhysida species to 23. Reported 20 October 2026.

q: Which country's army is exercising with the Indian Army at AUSTRAHIND 2026 in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala?
exp: The 5th edition of the India-Australia exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 runs from 19 October to 1 November 2026, with about 120 personnel from each side. Reported 19 October 2026.

q: Of all the stars, which one is closest to the Earth?
exp: At about 150 million kilometres away, the Sun is Earth's closest star; the next nearest, Proxima Centauri, is far farther still. The Moon is not a star, and Mars is a planet.

q: India's national anthem began as a Bengali poem by a Nobel Prize-winning writer. Who wrote it?
exp: The anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' comes from Rabindranath Tagore's Bengali poem 'Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata'; its first stanza was adopted on 24 January 1950. The national song 'Vande Mataram' is by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: A UNESCO tentative-list nomination reported on 20 October 2026 covers the archaeological landscape of Sirpur village, in Mahasamund district. In which state does it lie?
exp: The nomination, reported on 20 October 2026, is for the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh's Mahasamund district, on the Mahanadi river; the site is also a nationally protected monument.
